== Build notes: 2008 consolation results and source checks ==

Added 13th in both the Saturday consolation on 5 January 2008 and the Sunday consolation on 6 January 2008, using [[Premiere - Original VS14]]. Neither entry is marked dropped in its numbered standings.<ref>[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=18352#p255191 Saturday consolation standings], Players Committee Forums.</ref><ref>[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=18322#p254691 Sunday consolation standings], Players Committee Forums.</ref>

=== Possibly faulty data: event stage and finish ===

The former 2020 Texas Mini Worlds Top 8 finish of 4 conflicts with the actual bracket: Joe Olson faced Kafer in the Round of 8, then Olson appeared in the Final 4. The row now says Quarterfinalist. The separate Round of 16 row says Advanced to quarterfinals rather than repeating an unsupported unique finish of 7. The Top 8 Dark Side link now points to the existing ISB Operations article, matching the actual Elite 8 deck publication; the Carbon Chamber Testing deck belongs to the pod listing.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2020-texas-mini-worlds/ 2020 Texas Mini Worlds], Players Committee, Matchplay Results.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2020-tmw-elite-8-bill-kafer-ds-isb/ Elite 8 Bill Kafer DS ISB], Players Committee.</ref> The existing ISB deck article adds virtual qualifiers to Admiral Ozzel and Corporal Oberk that the native list does not explicitly print. Those two card-state qualifiers remain a separate deck-accuracy question; no deck article or card identity was changed by this profile edit.

For the 2022 Endor Grand Prix, the PC list numbers Kafer 6 among the Top 8. The live Day 2 report pairs him with Joe Olson and records Olson advancing, so the match-play row now says Quarterfinalist rather than a unique final 5th. The separate Day 1 row remains 6; seeding and elimination stage should not be conflated.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2022-endor-grand-prix/ 2022 Endor Grand Prix], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=80655#p1374509 Day 2 updates], Players Committee Forums.</ref>

The former 2016 Texas Mini Worlds 9 and 2019 North American Continentals 18 finishes are blank pending actual placing evidence. The cited pages list the decks after the numbered leaders without an explicit placing for Kafer; list position alone is not a rank. Participation and all existing deck links remain. The 2016 individual Dark Side publication starts Endor Operations and includes That Thing’s Operational, so the event index's TTO shorthand does not require changing the existing Endor Operations link.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2016-texas-mini-worlds/ 2016 Texas Mini Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2016-texas-mini-worlds-bill-kafer-day-1-ds/ Bill Kafer Day 1 DS], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2019-north-american-continentals/ 2019 North American Continentals], Players Committee.</ref>

The 2020 Worlds Day 2 31st is genuinely supported by the rendered ordered standings and remains. The explicitly numbered 2021 U.S. Nationals 32nd and 2026 San Diego Day 2 5th remain. The LOTR 2010 15th also remains: its source is explicitly headed Final Standings, with 16 entries sorted by points and differential; Kafer is the fifteenth entry, with 4 points and a dropped notation. This is a position in declared final standings, not an inferred rank from a deck catalogue.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2020-world-championships/ 2020 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2021-us-nationals/ 2021 U.S. Nationals], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2026-04-san-diego-super-open-san-diego-california-apr-11-to-12-2026/ 2026 San Diego Super Open], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://lotrtcgwiki.com/forums/index.php?topic=5072.30 LOTR Worlds Event 2010], The Last Homely House, final standings post, 22 September 2010.</ref>

=== Historical source-copy provenance ===

The earlier 2010 forum index contains no post-body placing proof. The 2011 forum board requires a registered login; no account access was attempted. The article instead cites the actual public original PDFs, whose full bytes match the independently backed Wiki copies: 2010 Day 2 p. 55 and 2011 Day 2 p. 64 identify Kafer's Dark Side sheets. The 2012 Alderaan old download URL returned an access-block page, so its byte identity remains unproven. The article cites the actual recovered historical Wiki PDF, p. 8, naming TacoBill and Set Your Course For Alderaan. This does not assert equality with that older origin. The former source URLs and values remain in [[Special:PermanentLink/322310|revision 322310]] and the independently backed provenance ledger.

The present public Google roster grid explicitly lists Bill Kafer, TacoBill and New Allies. That checked visible grid is preserved as a current browser document, separately from the existing 14 September 2025 text copy; no workbook or historical byte identity was inferred. Existing images, their lead choice, and the public roster text remain unchanged. Every current native version was checked against independent Git backups. Current DeckTech recasts and archival reconstructions are labeled as those representations, not as original-era HTTP captures. Capture work remains pending with the existing preservation owner; these publication checks do not declare all preservation complete.

The remaining Bill Kafer entries were compared with the already-preserved PC sources. Six more inherited finish cells were catalogue positions rather than stated results: 2017 MPC 34 and 2018 MPC 24 are in surname-alphabetical Day 1 deck lists; 2017 U.S. Nationals 10 follows an unnumbered alphabetical remainder after the numbered Top 8; 2016 Worlds 16 is an unnumbered Day 1 deck position. Both 2020 Endor Grand Prix rows formerly showed 6, matching the sixth entry in separate unnumbered Day 1 and Day 2 deck lists. These six cells are now blank; all event, format and deck rows remain. No lower finish or tied placement was invented.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/match-play-championship/ 2017 MPC], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2018-match-play-championships/ 2018 MPC], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/tournament-decklists/ Tournament decklists], Players Committee, 2017 U.S. Nationals section.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2016-world-championships/ 2016 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2020-endor-grand-prix/ 2020 Endor Grand Prix], Players Committee.</ref>

=== 2016 Worlds stage conflict ===
The event index places Kafer's Coruscant CR(V)/TRM pair under Day 1, outside its separate eight-player Day 2 list. However, its linked original PC deck locators themselves say day-2-bill-kafer, as do the existing Wiki deck articles. The profile's existing Day 2 wording and deck links are retained pending direct historical resolution. The former 16 is not established as a Day 2 result. No deck article has been renamed to settle this conflict by assumption.

=== Positive placing evidence retained ===
The 2015 Worlds 23rd and 2015 San Diego Grand Prix 29th are retained: although the visible catalogue lines do not print the numbers, their actual original PC deck links explicitly contain 23rd-place and 29th-place. This is different from inferring a place from list position.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2015-world-championships/ 2015 Worlds], Players Committee, Kafer's linked 23rd-place deck publications.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2015-san-diego-grand-prix/ 2015 San Diego Grand Prix], Players Committee, Kafer's linked 29th-place deck publications.</ref> The explicitly printed 2017 Worlds 40 and 2018 Worlds 20 also remain, as do the numbered 2023 Worlds 8, 2024 North American Continentals Top 8 3 and Day 1 2, 2026 Worlds Day 1 31, and 2021 Dagobah/Yavin 4 Regionals 3/2.<ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2017-world-championships/ 2017 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2018-world-championships/ 2018 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2023-07-world-championships-morristown-new-jersey-aug-11-13/ 2023 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2024-08-north-american-continental-championship-new-brunswick-new-jersey-august-9-112024/ 2024 North American Continentals], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2026-11-swccg-world-championship-bloomington-minnesota-oct-23-25-2026/ 2026 Worlds], Players Committee.</ref><ref>[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2021-regional-championships/ 2021 Regionals], Players Committee.</ref>
